advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard record_parent_divergence's append with alert_store.is_deduped on a stable dedup key (e.g. f"{kind}:{key}:{parent}") so a persistent parent divergence does not re-file every pass.
evidence: pass_io.py:133 `_load_alert_store().append({...})` is called unconditionally with no dedup key
alert_store.py:62 `def is_deduped(key: str, repo_root: Path, window_ns: int = _24H_NS) -> bool:` exists precisely for this
fetcher.py:200-202 docstring: 'de-duplicates the observable alert across passes via alert_store.is_deduped (24h window) so a persistent unmapped status does not re-file every ~20-minute pass'
fetcher.py:225 `if not alert_store.is_deduped(dedup_key, repo_root=repo_root): alert_store.append(...)` — the established pattern for persistent divergences
The ticket notes the differ 're-emitted the identical parent mutation on every pass (~230 steady-state mutations)', so an unrepresentable parent recurs every pass
advisory.finding: record_parent_divergence appends a bridge_alerts entry on every pass with no is_deduped guard, so a persistent parent divergence (especially outbound-parent-unrepresentable, where 'no retry helps') re-files an alert on every ~20-minute reconcile pass, growing the store unboundedly and flooding the operator's divergence channel.
scenarios: A DC deployment with one genuinely unrepresentable parent runs the reconcile loop for days: bridge_alerts accrues one identical outbound-parent-unrepresentable record per issue per pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute a dedup_key (e.g. f"{kind}:{key}:{parent}") and wrap the append in `if not store.is_deduped(dedup_key, repo_root=repo_root):`, writing that key as the record's "key" so is_deduped can match it across passes.
